headline: Profit growth continues on loan growth, better credit trends
summary_short: First Horizon's net income available to common shareholders rose 12% y/y and 1% q/q to $260M ($0.54 diluted EPS, +20% y/y), as net interest income grew on loan growth even though the margin slipped 3bp to 3.49%, while credit quality kept improving and CET1 held at 10.5%.
summary_long: Net interest income (FTE) rose $9M q/q to $679M on loan-portfolio growth, while NIM slipped 3bp to 3.49% as higher deposit costs from increased brokered deposits offset the gain. Noninterest income grew $16M q/q to $211M, led by deferred-compensation income and brokerage/trust/insurance, partly offset by a $7M fixed-income decline. Noninterest expense rose $26M to $531M on higher outside-services and deferred-compensation costs. Provision for credit losses held flat at $15M; net charge-offs ticked up to 20bp of loans, but nonperforming loans fell $75M and the allowance-to-loans ratio improved to 1.24%. CET1 held steady at 10.5%; the bank repurchased $100M of stock. Effective tax rate fell to 19.5% from 22.2%. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Net interest income rose $9M q/q on loan-portfolio growth; noninterest income rose $16M q/q on deferred-compensation income and brokerage/trust/insurance, partly offset by a $7M fixed-income decline.
Revenue growth outpaced the $26M q/q rise in noninterest expense, provision for credit losses held flat at $15M, and the effective tax rate fell to 19.5% from 22.2%.
Follows from higher net income against a lower diluted share count (480M vs 487M q/q, 514M y/y); the release notes share count in all periods was impacted by share repurchases.
Same net income growth and repurchase-driven share-count decline as diluted EPS.
Roughly unchanged q/q as the $26M rise in noninterest expense (outside services, deferred compensation) offset revenue growth; up 10% y/y on stronger revenue and a lower credit-loss provision.

Combined shareholders' equity was roughly unchanged q/q ($9,168M vs $9,170M) as retained-earnings growth was offset by $100M of share repurchases and a wider accumulated-other-comprehensive-loss balance; up 2.3% y/y on cumulative retained-earnings growth.
CEO Bryan Jordan framed the quarter as "disciplined execution" driven by client relationships and service; first-half 2026 NIAC grew 16% y/y including 3% y/y loan growth.
